name: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis
definition: Displacement through the proximal femoral physis in adolescents, often presenting with hip, groin, thigh or knee pain and limp.

typical: Obligate external rotation with hip flexion

redFlags.item: Inability to bear weight suggesting unstable SCFE

investigations.principle: Urgent imaging is required when suspected.
investigations.MRI: MRI can detect pre-slip changes in selected cases.
investigations.radiographs: AP and frog-leg lateral radiographs are typical for stable cases; avoid frog-leg positioning in unstable SCFE.

amber: Manipulative reduction should be avoided; unstable SCFE carries high AVN risk.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Asthi/Sandhi developmental pathology may be documented in parallel only.

patientEducation.summary: Displacement through the proximal femoral physis in adolescents, often presenting with hip, groin, thigh or knee pain and limp.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
